title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: The 2026-07-28 MCP spec is now landing in Claude — stateless core plus connector observability, enterprise-managed auth, embedded UI, and private network tunnels
bullets.summary: Claude expands support for the fifth MCP spec: a request/response stateless core (remote servers run serverless/edge behind a plain load balancer), stronger OAuth/OIDC, versioned Apps/Tasks extensions, and first-class connector features — embedded UI, org-managed auth, observability, private tunnels; 950+ servers in the directory, MCP past 400M monthly SDK downloads.
bullets.how: This is the deployment + governance layer for The Construct's own MCP fleet: stateless lets our internal servers go serverless/horizontally scaled, and built-in observability + enterprise-managed auth + private tunnels are exactly the control plane to run the fleet safely instead of hand-rolling it.

bullets.title: Anthropic runtime shift still the substrate — Cowork on web + mobile with offline background tasks and phone-approval, doubled usage limits through Aug 5
bullets.summary: Scheduled Cowork tasks now run even when none of the user's devices are online and push a phone notification when something needs review or approval; usage shows most Cowork users aren't coding.
bullets.how: The layer this Pulse scan itself runs on; our scheduled operators are now always-on background workers with a human-approval gate on the phone. Pair with item 1: offline-survivable, approval-gated tasks running on stateless, observable connectors.

bullets.title: Frontier stays seated on capability, war moves to unit cost — OpenAI cut Luna -80% / Terra -20% on Jul 30; Gemini 3.6 Flash and the GPT-5.6 line are the cheap workhorses
bullets.summary: No new frontier tier cleared the 24h bar; Opus 5 (Jul 24) remains the newest reasoning tier while the everyday/bulk tiers keep repricing downward after the Jul 30 cut.
bullets.how: Hold Opus 5 for reasoning-heavy Construct jobs, route high-volume bulk to Luna/Flash and re-check the routing math after the Jul 30 cut; no top-tier switch this cycle.

bullets.title: Vertical-MCP wave keeps rotating creative/ad surfaces in — GetHookd ships an API + MCP server for AI-powered ecommerce ad research (Jul 31)
bullets.summary: GetHookd exposes ad-research and creative-generation as agent-callable tools: pull competitor ad creative and generate new concepts from a plain-language request across any MCP client.
bullets.how: A paid-media/creative surface adjacent to Brand 9 Signs' output; wire it into one Construct creative-and-paid-media operator alongside the media MCPs already flagged (VEED, Higgsfield), don't resell it standalone.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'Generative Skill Composition for LLM Agents' (2606.32025) + SkillBench
bullets.summary: Frames capability as composed skills rather than monolithic prompts, with a benchmark of multi-skill synthetic tasks covering compositions of 2-5 skills — how well an agent chains skills it already holds.
bullets.how: Direct framework for our new-skills scan and installed-skills registry: the value isn't the count of skills, it's composability; score and promote skills by how well they compose, not just whether they trigger.

praxis_lesson: Two Anthropic layers now converge into one operating discipline for The Construct: the 2026-07-28 stateless MCP spec (serverless deploy + built-in observability, enterprise-managed auth, private tunnels) is the control plane, and Cowork's offline background-task + phone-approval model is the runtime. Stop hand-rolling fleet plumbing — run our internal MCP servers stateless-and-observable on managed auth, run our operators as offline-survivable, approval-gated Cowork tasks, and per 2606.32025 treat the skill registry as a composability graph to be scored and promoted, not a static list. Own the control-plane + runtime discipline, not any single generator or feed.
